papers.title: The Emotional Dog and Its Rational Tail: A Social Intuitionist Approach to Moral Judgment
papers.abstract_snippet: Foundational paper arguing that moral judgments are driven primarily by quick moral intuitions, with moral reasoning serving mainly as post-hoc rationalization. Proposes the social intuitionist model with six links between intuition, judgment, and reasoning.

papers.title: Moral Dumbfounding: When Intuition Finds No Reason
papers.authors: Haidt, J., Bjorklund, F., & Murphy, S.
papers.abstract_snippet: Demonstrates moral dumbfounding — people maintain strong moral judgments about harmless taboo violations even when they cannot articulate reasons, providing key evidence for the primacy of intuition over reasoning in moral judgment.

papers.title: Intuitive Ethics: How Innately Prepared Intuitions Generate Culturally Variable Virtues
papers.abstract_snippet: Proposes that humans come equipped with innate preparedness to feel moral intuitions about suffering, hierarchy, reciprocity, and purity, which then generate culturally variable virtues through social learning.

papers.title: The Righteous Mind: Why Good People Are Divided by Politics and Religion
papers.abstract_snippet: Book-length treatment of Moral Foundations Theory and the social intuitionist model. Argues that morality is built on innate foundations, moral reasoning is mostly post-hoc, and ideological divides stem from differential weighting of moral foundations.

papers.title: A roadmap for evaluating moral competence in large language models
papers.abstract_snippet: Proposes a comprehensive roadmap for evaluating moral competence in LLMs, arguing that current benchmarks are insufficient and outlining key dimensions including moral perception, judgment, reasoning, and action.

papers.title: The Preference for Indirect Harm
papers.abstract_snippet: Examines the psychological basis of the preference for indirect over direct harm in moral judgment, showing that moral intuitions track causal and intentional features of harmful actions.

papers.title: Social Intuitionists Answer Six Questions about Morality
papers.venue: Chapter in Moral Psychology Vol 2 (MIT Press)
papers.abstract_snippet: Addresses six fundamental questions about morality from the social intuitionist perspective, defending and extending the model against rationalist critiques. Clarifies the role of reasoning as interpersonal persuasion.

papers.title: The Role of Conscious Reasoning and Intuition in Moral Judgment: Testing Three Principles of Harm
papers.authors: Cushman, F., Young, L., & Hauser, M.
papers.abstract_snippet: Tests three principles underlying moral judgments about harm: the action principle, the intention principle, and the contact principle. Shows that intuitive judgments align with these principles even when people cannot articulate them.

papers.title: Insights into Moral Reasoning of AI
papers.abstract_snippet: Examines the moral reasoning capabilities of AI systems through the lens of social intuitionism and moral foundations theory, analyzing how LLMs process and respond to moral scenarios.

papers.title: Beyond Verdicts: Evaluating Language Model Moral Competence
papers.abstract_snippet: Argues that evaluating LLM moral competence requires going beyond simple verdict accuracy to assess reasoning quality, consistency, and sensitivity to morally relevant features.

papers.title: Robustness of large language models in moral judgements
papers.abstract_snippet: Tests the robustness of LLM moral judgments under various perturbations, finding significant sensitivity to framing effects that parallel known human cognitive biases in moral cognition.

papers.title: AI language model rivals expert ethicist in moral reasoning
papers.abstract_snippet: Compares LLM moral reasoning performance to expert ethicists, finding that advanced language models can approximate expert-level moral reasoning in structured ethical scenarios.
